The '''DH-17 blaster carbine''', otherwise known as the '''DH-17 Carbine''', or sometimes unhyphenated as the '''DH17 carbine''', was a heavier version of the [[DH-17 blaster pistol/Legends|DH-17 blaster pistol]] produced by [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]]. This [[Blaster carbine/Legends|blaster carbine]] saw heavy use by both the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] throughout the course of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], due to its durability and versatility.

==Description==
The DH-17 [[Blaster carbine/Legends|blaster carbine]] served as the heavier cousin of the widely popular [[DH-17 blaster pistol/Legends|DH-17 blaster pistol]] used by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]],<ref name="FiB" /> weighing over 1 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilogram]].<ref name="Weight" /> As a more streamlined variant of the popular [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]], the DH-17 Carbine sported a number of practical and cosmetic differences, notably the absence of a [[Scope/Legends|scope]] like the one seen on its lighter counterpart.<ref name="TCG">{{SWGTCG|set=Squadrons Over Corellia|cardname=DH-17 Carbine}}</ref> Much like the [[Pistol/Legends|pistol]] variation, the DH-17 [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] carbine was powerful enough to penetrate most personal [[Armor/Legends|armor]], but it lacked the ability to breach bulkheads and [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Hull/Legends|hulls]], making it ideal for shipboard skirmishes.<ref name="FiB" /> While most basic DH-17 Carbine's featured a [[Color/Legends|silver-colored]] [[Barrel/Legends|barrel]], some retrofitted versions were entirely black. The weapon was comprised of various materials, including units of ferrous and non-ferrous metal, as well as [[Polymer/Legends|polymer]]. In addition to a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] barrel, DH-17 Carbine's were manufactured with a ranged weapon core, and the carbine could be optionally fitted with a scope and [[Stock/Legends|stock]].<ref name="SWG" /> The carbine was capable of firing at a medium range, and had both a [[Stun/Legends|stun]] setting and auto-fire capabilities.<ref name="FiB" /> The weapon closely resembled the [[CDEF carbine]], a weapon favored by the [[Corellian Security Force]].<ref name="SWG" />

==History==
[[File:BasicDH17.png|250px|thumb|A basic DH-17 blaster carbine]]
[[File:RetrofittedBlackDH17Carbine.png|250px|thumb|A retrofitted black DH-17 Carbine]]
The blaster carbine variant of the DH-17 saw heavy use by both the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] and the Alliance to Restore the Republic throughout the course of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Lauded for its durability and versatility, it became a mainstay with [[Rebel trooper/Legends|Rebel soldiers]] due to its simple design and the wide availability of replacement parts on the [[Black market/Legends|black market]]. [[Rebel Marine|Rebel marines]] often installed a spread barrel modification to make it a deck sweeper commonly referred to as the [[DH-17 short carbine]]. That, combined with the DH-17's auto-fire capabilities, allowed [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] to blanket an entire starship corridor with blaster fire.<ref name="FiB" />

The weapon was suitable for novice [[Sniper/Legends|marksmen]], and polished black versions were favored by [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], [[Commando/Legends|commandos]], and [[Spy/Legends|spies]].<ref name="SWG" /> In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> Rebel Alliance [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|hero]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] provided a DH-17 Carbine to at least one intrepid [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] rescued from an [[Unidentified Imperial space station|Imperial space station]].<ref name="SWG:YNW">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|You Need Work|Tansarii Point Station}}</ref> A skilled marksman by the name of [[Loche Crestingsky]] also possessed a DH-17 Carbine of his own while staying aboard [[Tansarii Point Station/Legends|Tansarii Point Station]] in the [[Bright Jewel system/Legends|Bright Jewel System]].<ref name="SWG:StS">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Stopping the Slicers|Tansarii Point Station}}</ref> While the carbine was primarily manufactured by [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech Industries]]<ref name="BlasTechExplain" /> for a standard price of 900 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="FiB" /> schematics of the weapon were also available to independent [[weaponsmith]]s<ref name="SWG" /> and [[Merchant/Legends|munitions traders]].<ref name="SWG:SK">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The [[W:c:swg:DH17 Carbine|DH-17 blaster carbine]] was included as a [[W:c:swg:Carbine|carbine]] in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', a [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]],<ref name="SWG" /> prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> The [[W:c:swg:Weapon|weapon]] could be [[W:c:swg:Crafting|crafted]] by [[W:c:swg:Weaponsmith (pre NGE)|weaponsmiths]] and used by novice players of the [[W:c:swg:Marksman|marksman]] [[W:c:swg:Professions (pre-NGE)|profession]].<ref name="SWG" /> Following the release of [[W:c:swg:Publish 25 Notes for November 15 2005|Publish 25's]] [[W:c:swg:New Game Enhancements|New Game Enhancements]] on [[November 15]], [[2005]], weaponsmiths were removed,<ref name="NGE">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref> however the weapon could still be constructed by players of the newly created [[W:c:swg:Trader (Munitions)|munitions trader]] [[W:c:swg:Profession|profession]]. The weapon could be constructed using a number of different [[W:c:swg:Ranged weapon component|components]] and [[W:c:swg:Resource|resources]], including [[W:c:swg:Ferrous metal|ferrous]] and [[W:c:swg:Non-ferrous metal|non-ferrous metal]], and [[W:c:swg:Polymer|polymer]].<ref name="SWG:SK" />

As part of the [[W:c:swg:New Player Tutorial|New Player Tutorial]] featuring [[W:c:swg:Tansarii Point Station|Tansarii Point Station]],<ref name="NGE" /> [[W:c:swg:Han Solo|Han Solo]] would give players of the [[W:c:swg:Bounty Hunter|bounty hunter]], [[W:c:swg:Commando|commando]], and [[W:c:swg:Spy|spy]] professions a polished black version of the DH-17.<ref name="SWG:YNW" /> Players could also choose to receive Loche Crestingsky's DH-17 carbine by completing the [[W:c:swg:Quest|quest]] "[[W:c:swg:Stopping the Slicers|Stopping the Slicers]]" aboard Tansarii Point Station.<ref name="SWG:StS" /> In ''[[Squadrons Over Corellia]]'', the first expansion of the ''[[Star Wars Galaxies Trading Card Game]]'' released on [[December 16]], [[2008]], the DH-17 Carbine was introduced as a game [[W:c:swg:Card list|card]]. The artwork for the carbine illustration was completed by [[Keun Chul Jang]].<ref name="TCG" /><ref name="CreditsTCG">{{SonyCite|url=tradingcardgame/help/credits.vm|text=''Star Wars Galaxies'' TCG Credits}}</ref> Capitalization and hyphenation of the weapon's name was somewhat inconsistent between and within sources. In [[W:c:swg:Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies'']] alone, the weapon was referred to in various descriptions as a DH-17 Carbine, DH17 Carbine, DH17 carbine, or simply as a DH-17.<ref name="SWG" /> The [[Fantasy Flight Games]] sourcebook ''[[Forged in Battle]]'', released on [[August 18]], [[2016]], provides the full name of DH-17 blaster carbine.<ref name="FiB" />
